_comment: THE 2002 CONTENT-KEYED MANIFEST (kb/Work PB5256): the clauses of specs/ISO_COBOL_2002.md whose body carries an
ascending numbered list under a heading that names no rule block, as extract_rule_catalog.py's scan measures them
(`ordinal_shape`), in the shape of the 2023 manifest (spec-unharvested-rule-blocks.json, whose comment states each
key). A disposition is an adjudication by §2002:5.2.1 (a syntax rule) and §2002:5.2.2 (a general rule), never a
guess. Seeded on 2026-11-11: a clause whose list body was word for word (cite.norm) the text of exactly one 2023
manifest clause with the same ordinal count would have carried that clause's disposition; none of the 92 is, so
every one is `pending`, and its rules are not in the 2002 denominator until it is adjudicated. `candidate` is the
adjudicator's starting point, never a disposition: the 2023 manifest clause of the same title nearest in text
(difflib ratio over the cite.norm words), with its disposition and kind. `paragraph-blocks` (prose clauses
admitted one row per paragraph, 2023's 9.1.16 to 9.1.18) is empty: no 2002 clause of the same title has the
same prose, so each is adjudicated with the rest. The 2002 transcription is not reconciled yet (kb/Work PB4813):
a correction that moves a clause's list drifts it here, and extract_rule_catalog.py --edition 2002 --check names it.
